extracted.intended_audience: generic drug manufacturers, regulatory and IP professionals, policy analysts
extracted.subtask_short: filing ANDA with paragraph IV certification
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing and submitting an Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) containing a paragraph IV patent certification under the Hatch‑Waxman framework, and the procedural and timing consequences (notification, litigation window, stays, and potential 180‑day exclusivity). Useful for generic applicants and their advisers assessing clearance and litigation strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Certify in its ANDA that the patent in question is invalid or is not infringed by the generic product (known as “paragraph IV certification”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is made as part of the ANDA submission and is the formal basis for seeking FDA approval before patent expiration. Making a paragraph IV certification will typically provoke patent-holder enforcement actions and is the trigger for the Hatch‑Waxman procedures described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of patent holder
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify the patent holder of the submission of the ANDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ANDA applicant must serve notice to the patent owner after filing the paragraph IV certification; this notification starts the statutory deadlines (e.g., the patent holder’s 45‑day window to sue). Proper and timely notification is therefore a procedural prerequisite to invoking the litigation and stay provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: First filer 180‑day exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The first company to submit an Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) with the FDA has the exclusive right to market the generic drug for 180 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 180‑day exclusivity is a powerful commercial incentive for generic manufacturers to be the first to file a paragraph IV ANDA and can drive pre‑emptive filings and litigation strategy; exclusivity entitlement depends on being the first to file and on prevailing procedural/antitrust/patent challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent holder 45‑day window to sue
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent holder files an infringement suit against the generic applicant within 45 days of the ANDA notification, certain consequences follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 45‑day filing window is jurisdictionally critical: filing suit within this period triggers the automatic stay of FDA approval. Failure to file within 45 days may forfeit the ability to obtain the 30‑month stay tied to Hatch‑Waxman procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic 30‑month stay of FDA approval upon timely suit
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA approval to market the generic drug is automatically postponed for 30 months if the patent holder files suit within 45 days of ANDA notification, unless the patent expires or is judged to be invalid or not infringed before that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30‑month stay provides the patent holder time to litigate its infringement/validity claims in court before generic market entry; it can be shortened if the court decides the patent is invalid/not infringed or if the patent term expires during the stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA listing on FDA website
rubrics_metrics.description: ANDA applications containing a paragraph IV patent certification are listed on the FDA website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public listing provides transparency about pending paragraph IV challenges and can be used to monitor competitors’ filings and exclusivity status. See FDA resources titled 'Paragraph IV Patent Certifications' and 'Paragraph IV Drug Product Applications: Generic Drug Patent Challenge Notifications' for current listings and procedural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory framework: Hatch‑Waxman (Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process described operates under the Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act, or the Hatch‑Waxman Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understandings and remedies (paragraph IV certifications, 180‑day exclusivity, notice, 45‑day window, 30‑month stay) arise from this statute and associated FDA implementing procedures and case law; compliance requires aligning ANDA strategy with statutory and regulatory requirements.
